newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal Buddhists seek security after monk murder.
newsitem.headline: Nepal Buddhists seek security after monk murder.

text.p: Nepal's Buddhist organizations have called for tighter security after the mysterious murder of a Japanese monk at the spot believed to be the birthplace of Buddha, Buddhist leaders said on Saturday.
They condemned the incident on Thursday, when unidentified gunmen shot dead Yonataka Nawatami at Lumbini, 350 km (220 miles) west of Kathmandu near the Indian border.

"The brutal act committed inside the place where Lord Buddha, the apostle of peace was born, is a shame on humanity," an official of the Lumbini Development Trust, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The trust, which coordinates the work of international religious organizations working in the area, demanded additional security arrangements at the sacred place, he said.
One person was injured and six were taken into custody after the monk's murder, state radio said on Friday. Officials said they had no firm indication on the murderers or their motives.
Foreign religious institutions are building monastries or dome-shaped shrines, called "stupas," at Lumbini.

Lord Buddha was born a prince in the region now situated in Nepal, and later preached in the neighbouring regions after his enlightenment in the town of Gaya in the eastern Indian state of Bihar, bordering Nepal.
Nawatame was supervising the construction of a peace "pagoda," a temple tower being built by a Japanese religious organization, Nipponzan Myohoji.
Nepal's deputy prime minister Vam Dev Gautam, who is also the Home (interior) Minister, assured parliament on Friday of action to identify and punish the murderers.
